name: Dublin
intro: Dublin weddings sit at the higher end of the Irish market, a mix of grand city hotels, country-house venues just outside the M50, and converted warehouse-style spaces in the city itself. The bar for a wedding band in Dublin is high: couples have seen good live music and won't accept thin backing-track sets.
venues: Powerscourt House (just over the Wicklow border)
Tankardstown House (just over the Meath border)
travelNote: Most wedding bands are either based in Dublin or travelling in from surrounding counties, so the run to a Dublin venue is rarely more than ninety minutes door to door. City-centre hotels and converted spaces add loading-bay and parking headaches that country houses do not, and a late finish can mean a slow crawl out of town or a city hotel night rather than a same-day return home.

venueNotes.name: Powerscourt House (just over the Wicklow border)
venueNotes.note: A grand country-house setting with multiple rooms; the band will need clarity on which entrance and lift route is approved for load-in.

venueNotes.name: Carton House
venueNotes.note: Estate scale means a long walk from car park to ballroom; confirm whether the venue provides a trolley or allows closer access for equipment.

venueNotes.name: The Westbury
venueNotes.note: Central-city luxury with tight loading windows; evening parking is limited, so bands usually factor extra time for set-down.

venueNotes.name: The Marker
venueNotes.note: A modern, design-led space in the docklands with good lift access but a specific after-hours route; worth confirming load-out times in advance.

venueNotes.name: Tankardstown House (just over the Meath border)
venueNotes.note: A short run from Dublin with a rural, boutique feel; the band can usually same-day it unless the finish is very late.

localFaq.q: Do Dublin wedding bands charge extra for city-centre parking and loading?
localFaq.a: Most bands include a modest travel allowance within Dublin, but city-centre venues with paid parking or controlled loading bays can add a small surcharge; it's worth asking for this in the quote.

localFaq.q: Can a band set up early in a Dublin hotel ballroom before the reception?
localFaq.a: Many city hotels schedule multiple events, so an early sound check isn't guaranteed; bands usually plan a discrete line-check during room turnaround.

localFaq.q: Is a late licence common at Dublin wedding venues?
localFaq.a: City and hotel venues vary widely; some have late licences until the small hours, while others require music to finish earlier, so confirm the curfew before you book.

planningNote: Dublin's wedding season runs strongest from April through October, with Saturday dates in May, June and September booking out well over a year ahead. Friday and Sunday slots are increasingly popular as couples look for availability and better rates, while mid-winter weddings remain less common but easier to secure.

name: Cork
intro: Cork wedding venues are a balance of coastal, country-house, and city luxury, Castlemartyr, Fota Island, Ballymaloe, Hayfield Manor. The county's wedding scene rewards musicianship; Cork couples tend to choose live bands over DJ-only receptions at a higher rate than the national average.
travelNote: A Dublin band driving to Cork faces a solid two-and-a-half to three hours on the M7 and M8, so most treat it as a full travel day and often prefer an overnight, especially if the finish is after midnight. Cork-based bands cover the county easily, with most venues within an hour of the city, but coastal locations like Baltimore or Kinsale can still add time on narrow roads.

venueNotes.name: Castlemartyr Resort
venueNotes.note: A large resort with a dedicated ballroom; load-in is straightforward but the walk from the car park can be long, so trolleys help.

venueNotes.name: Fota Island Resort
venueNotes.note: Spread across the island estate, so confirm exactly which building and entrance the band should use.

venueNotes.name: Ballymaloe House
venueNotes.note: A farmhouse-country-house feel with a more intimate room; the stage area is modest, so a compact band line-up suits it best.

venueNotes.name: Hayfield Manor
venueNotes.note: City-centre manor house with a smaller, refined ballroom; good for an acoustic-led or scaled-back setup.

venueNotes.name: Castle Lyons
venueNotes.note: A village venue with character; parking is generally easy but check whether the band can load close to the performance space.

localFaq.q: Do bands from Dublin charge travel fees for Cork weddings?
localFaq.a: Yes, most Dublin-based bands add a travel fee for Cork to cover fuel and the longer day; Cork-based bands may not charge travel within the county.

localFaq.q: Should we book accommodation for the band in Cork?
localFaq.a: For late finishes or venues more than an hour from the band's base, an overnight room is often appreciated and sometimes written into the contract.

localFaq.q: Can we have our ceremony and reception at the same Cork venue?
localFaq.a: Many Cork hotels and country houses offer both, which simplifies logistics; just confirm the room flip and sound-check timing with the coordinator.

planningNote: Cork weddings peak from May through September, with coastal venues in particular filling fast for summer Saturdays. The county also has a strong off-season scene in manor houses and city hotels, though winter coastal weddings are quieter.

name: Galway
intro: Galway weddings split between west-of-Ireland castle settings (Ashford, Ballynahinch), city venues, and Connemara country houses. The atmosphere tends toward warm-and-loud rather than stately-and-quiet, which rewards bands that can build energy and hold a packed floor.
venues: Ashford Castle (just over the Mayo border)
travelNote: The M6 from Dublin gets a band to Galway city in roughly two to two-and-a-half hours, so city and nearby venues are often feasible as a same-day return. Connemara, the Aran-side coast and late finishes push most bands toward an overnight, especially when the route winds beyond Oughterard onto smaller roads.

venueNotes.name: Ashford Castle (just over the Mayo border)
venueNotes.note: One of Ireland's most exacting venues; the band will coordinate closely with the events team on load-in timing and room layout.

venueNotes.name: Glenlo Abbey
venueNotes.note: A country-estate hotel with a generous ballroom; access is good but confirm whether the reception is in the main house or the abbey.

venueNotes.name: Ballynahinch Castle
venueNotes.note: Remote Connemara setting with a warm, intimate room; the band usually needs overnight accommodation given the distance.

venueNotes.name: The Lough Rea Hotel
venueNotes.note: A convenient stop just off the Galway-Dublin road with straightforward loading and parking.

venueNotes.name: Cashel House
venueNotes.note: A quieter Connemara house with a smaller reception room; worth discussing the ideal band size for the space.

localFaq.q: How far in advance should we book a Galway wedding band?
localFaq.a: Summer Saturdays, especially around Race Week and bank holidays, book up quickly; aim to secure your band nine to twelve months ahead.

localFaq.q: Do bands need overnight accommodation for Connemara weddings?
localFaq.a: Yes, venues in Connemara or on the west coast are far enough from Dublin and Cork that an overnight room is standard.

localFaq.q: Are rural Galway venues reliable for power supply?
localFaq.a: Most established venues have ample power, but older country houses may need the band to bring a smaller PA or confirm socket locations during the site visit.

planningNote: Galway's wedding calendar is heavily weighted toward late spring through early autumn, with July and August especially busy due to visitors and festival weekends. September has become almost as sought-after as June for couples wanting softer light and fewer tourists.

name: Kerry
intro: Kerry's destination wedding scene is one of Ireland's most distinctive, Killarney lakeside venues, Dingle peninsula intimacy, the Park Hotel Kenmare's exclusivity. Travel matters here, both for guests and bands; couples value the kind of band that justifies the journey.
travelNote: From Dublin, a Kerry wedding means a four-to-four-and-a-half-hour run to Killarney and even longer to Dingle or the Beara side, so bands almost always need an overnight. Cork-based bands can reach Killarney in under two hours, but the Ring of Kerry and Dingle peninsula roads still demand extra time and careful routing.

venueNotes.name: Park Hotel Kenmare
venueNotes.note: A refined, compact ballroom in a stunning town; loading is via a discreet service entrance, best confirmed in advance.

venueNotes.name: Sheen Falls Lodge
venueNotes.note: Luxury country-house setting with a riverside location; the band usually needs overnight accommodation.

venueNotes.name: Muckross Park Hotel
venueNotes.note: A large Killarney hotel with good access; the main ballroom suits a full band and a lively dance floor.

venueNotes.name: Cahernane House
venueNotes.note: A Victorian mansion on the edge of Killarney National Park; load-in is manageable but the route is narrow.

venueNotes.name: Ballygarry Estate
venueNotes.note: Modern estate hotel with a dedicated events wing and straightforward parking.

localFaq.q: Is it harder to get a band to a Dingle peninsula wedding?
localFaq.a: The Conor Pass and narrow peninsula roads make Dingle a longer, slower journey, so bands generally allow extra travel time and may add a travel supplement.

localFaq.q: What should couples ask Kerry venues about managing sound levels?
localFaq.a: Some hotels and estates use sound management; rather than relying on hearsay, ask the venue directly what their policy is and share it with your band early.

localFaq.q: What time does the music usually finish in Kerry?
localFaq.a: Many Kerry hotels have standard late licences, but rural venues and residential areas can have earlier curfews; confirm the exact finish time before you book.

planningNote: Kerry's destination-wedding peak runs from May to October, with July and August Saturdays commanding the highest demand. Spring and late-autumn weddings can offer better availability and rates, though some coastal venues close or reduce capacity in winter.

name: Limerick
intro: Limerick is anchored by Adare Manor, one of Ireland's most exacting wedding venues, and complemented by Dromoland just over the Clare border. The Limerick wedding standard skews high; bands need to bring real musicianship rather than wedding-set autopilot.
travelNote: The M7 gets a Dublin band to Limerick in around two hours, and Cork is only ninety minutes to the south, so many Limerick weddings are same-day returns. Adare Manor and other rural estates can tip the balance toward an overnight if the finish is late or the load-out is drawn out.

venueNotes.name: Adare Manor
venueNotes.note: A five-star estate with very high production standards; the band will liaise with the in-house events team on timing and staging.

venueNotes.name: The Strand Hotel
venueNotes.note: A city-centre hotel with a modern ballroom and good loading access via the riverside.

venueNotes.name: Castletroy Park Hotel
venueNotes.note: Suburban hotel with generous function rooms and easy parking.

venueNotes.name: Glin Castle
venueNotes.note: A remote castle on the Shannon estuary; the band almost always stays overnight given the rural location.

localFaq.q: Do bands charge a travel fee for Limerick if they're coming from Dublin?
localFaq.a: Some Dublin bands include Limerick within their standard radius, while others add a travel fee; always confirm whether travel is included or itemised.

localFaq.q: Can the band play outdoors at a Limerick country house?
localFaq.a: Outdoor reception music is popular in summer, but you need a wet-weather backup and a power source; most bands will plan for an indoor setup as the default.

localFaq.q: Is parking easy for bands at Limerick city venues?
localFaq.a: City hotels generally have loading bays or nearby car parks, but it's worth reserving a space so the band isn't circling with heavy gear.

planningNote: Limerick weddings are busy from April through October, with Adare Manor setting the pace for premium dates. The county also sees strong corporate and international wedding traffic, which can make midweek dates at the top venues surprisingly competitive.

name: Mayo
intro: Mayo is Ashford Castle country, the flagship Irish destination wedding venue, set on the shores of Lough Corrib. Beyond Ashford, Mayo offers country-house and seaside-hotel options. The county's wedding scene draws couples from across Ireland and abroad.
travelNote: Dublin to Mayo is a three-to-three-and-a-half-hour haul to Castlebar or Westport, and the Atlantic coast adds another stretch on slower roads, so an overnight is normal. Galway bands are much closer, but venues near Achill or the north Mayo coast still require careful timing.

venueNotes.name: Ashford Castle
venueNotes.note: A destination venue with exacting standards; the band coordinates load-in and sound-check tightly with the events team.

venueNotes.name: Mount Falcon Estate
venueNotes.note: A country-house hotel with a warm ballroom; load-in is straightforward via the main courtyard.

venueNotes.name: Knockranny House Hotel
venueNotes.note: Westport town-centre location with good access and a lively wedding crowd.

venueNotes.name: The Ice House Hotel
venueNotes.note: A contemporary hotel on the river with compact function spaces; the band setup needs to suit a more intimate room.

localFaq.q: Do bands need to stay overnight for Mayo weddings?
localFaq.a: Most do, given the distance from Dublin and Cork and the reality of late finishes; the overnight room is usually discussed when you book.

localFaq.q: Are Westport and Castlebar easy for bands to reach?
localFaq.a: Yes, both towns are well connected, but the final stretch to rural or coastal venues can be narrow and slow, so bands build in extra time.

localFaq.q: What's the typical curfew for Mayo wedding venues?
localFaq.a: Town hotels often have later music licences, while rural venues may need to finish earlier; check the licence with the venue before signing.

planningNote: Mayo's wedding season runs from April through September, with Westport and the Ashford Castle area especially popular for summer Saturdays. Autumn can be beautiful along the coast, though weather contingency becomes more important for marquee or outdoor receptions.

name: Donegal
intro: Donegal weddings happen against some of Ireland's most dramatic coast and country backdrops. Lough Eske Castle leads the luxury end; the county also offers boutique and beach-adjacent options. Travel logistics matter, but a well-chosen band turns the journey north-west into part of the story.
travelNote: Donegal is one of the longest drives from Dublin, often three-and-a-half to four-and-a-half hours depending on whether the venue sits in the south of the county or up towards Dunfanaghy and the Atlantic coast, so bands almost always stay overnight. Belfast-based bands are closer for northern Donegal, but the Inishowen peninsula and remote coastal roads still demand a full travel day.

venueNotes.name: Lough Eske Castle
venueNotes.note: A five-star castle hotel with a dedicated events team; load-in routes and timings are planned in advance.

venueNotes.name: Harvey's Point
venueNotes.note: A lakeside hotel with an intimate, warmly lit ballroom; the room suits a band that can scale its energy to a smaller space.

venueNotes.name: Solis Lough Eske
venueNotes.note: A modern castle hotel with good access and a refined ballroom; confirm the specific entrance for load-in.

venueNotes.name: Rosapenna Hotel
venueNotes.note: A coastal resort on the Wild Atlantic Way; the band usually needs overnight accommodation given the distance.

localFaq.q: Is cross-border travel an issue for booking a band from the Republic for a Donegal wedding?
localFaq.a: Donegal is in the Republic, so there are no border checks for bands travelling from Dublin, Galway or Cork; just allow extra time for the long drive.

localFaq.q: Do bands charge more for remote Donegal venues?
localFaq.a: The distance and overnight stay mean most bands add a travel supplement; ask for this to be itemised in your quote.

localFaq.q: What should we ask Donegal venues about late finishes?
localFaq.a: Coastal and rural venues can have earlier noise curfews than city hotels; confirm the music finish time and any sound-management policy before you book.

planningNote: Donegal's wedding season is concentrated from May to September, with coastal and Wild Atlantic Way venues drawing couples from across Ireland and abroad. June and July are the busiest months, while autumn weddings can be stunning but require backup plans for Atlantic weather.

name: Wicklow
intro: Wicklow is Dublin's preferred wedding county, Powerscourt House dominates, complemented by Druids Glen, Tinakilly Country House, and Brooklodge. Estate-and-marquee venues dominate, which means bands need both refinement and party-band energy.
travelNote: Most Wicklow venues sit within thirty to ninety minutes of Dublin, making same-day returns the norm for bands based in the capital. Mountain and glen locations such as Brooklodge or the deeper Wicklow venues still need careful routing, especially after dark on narrow roads.

venueNotes.name: Powerscourt House
venueNotes.note: A grand Palladian house with a sweeping staircase; the band will need the approved load-in route, which is not the guest entrance.

venueNotes.name: Druids Glen
venueNotes.note: A resort with multiple event spaces; confirm which room is booked and where the band can park closest.

venueNotes.name: Tinakilly Country House
venueNotes.note: A Victorian country house with sea views; the ballroom is charming and suits a full live band.

venueNotes.name: Brooklodge
venueNotes.note: A mountain-valley hotel with a rustic feel; the drive in is winding, so bands allow extra time.

venueNotes.name: The Glenview
venueNotes.note: A family-run hotel with straightforward access and a welcoming wedding crowd.

localFaq.q: Is there an extra charge for a band to play in Wicklow?
localFaq.a: Because most Wicklow venues are close to Dublin, many bands include the county in their base rate; only the furthest mountain venues might attract a small supplement.

localFaq.q: Can the band set up outdoors at a Wicklow country house?
localFaq.a: Summer marquee receptions are popular, but you need a firm wet-weather plan and power for the PA; bands usually treat the indoor room as the main setup.

localFaq.q: How do late finishes work for bands travelling back to Dublin?
localFaq.a: Most Wicklow weddings finish late enough that a Dublin band can still be home in under two hours, so an overnight is rarely needed.

planningNote: Wicklow's wedding season mirrors Dublin's, peaking from May through September with Saturday dates at Powerscourt and Druids Glen booking out early. The county is also a popular choice for Friday and Sunday weddings because guests can stay over and enjoy the mountains or coast.

name: Clare
intro: Clare is anchored by Dromoland Castle and a coast of West Clare wedding hotels and houses, Vaughan Lodge, Old Ground, the Falls. The wedding crowd skews mixed-generation and the bands chosen reflect that: versatile, six-decade repertoires that suit both grandparents and the late-night dance floor.
travelNote: Dublin to Clare is a two-and-a-half to three-hour run to Ennis, with West Clare and the coast adding more time on smaller roads, so bands often stay overnight for coastal or late-finish weddings. Limerick and Galway bands are much closer, and Shannon Airport is handy for guests flying in.

venueNotes.name: Dromoland Castle
venueNotes.note: A five-star castle with a dedicated events team; the band coordinates closely on staging and timing.

venueNotes.name: Vaughan Lodge
venueNotes.note: A boutique coastal hotel with a compact, stylish room; a scaled-back band line-up often works best.

venueNotes.name: The Old Ground Hotel
venueNotes.note: A historic hotel in the centre of Ennis with good access and a lively wedding atmosphere.

venueNotes.name: Trump International (Doonbeg)
venueNotes.note: A coastal resort with high standards; load-in and parking arrangements should be confirmed in advance.

localFaq.q: Should we book accommodation for the band in Clare?
localFaq.a: For West Clare, the Burren or any late finish, an overnight room is standard; closer to Limerick or Ennis it may not be needed.

localFaq.q: Can we have a band at a small Clare boutique venue?
localFaq.a: Yes, but the room size and power need to match the band's footprint; many bands offer a compact acoustic option for smaller spaces.

localFaq.q: What should couples confirm with Clare venues about noise management?
localFaq.a: Some hotels and estates manage sound levels, particularly in residential or coastal areas; ask the venue directly about their policy and pass it to your band.

planningNote: Clare's wedding season runs strongest from April through September, with coastal venues around Lahinch and Doonbeg peaking in July and August. The county also draws couples for autumn weddings when the Burren light is at its best.

name: Tipperary
intro: Tipperary's wedding venues include Dundrum House, Ballyseede Castle (just over the Kerry border), and Cashel Palace, a careful balance of castle, country house, and historic-hotel style. The county's wedding scene leans toward warm, characterful celebrations rather than corporate polish.
travelNote: Dublin to north Tipperary is around an hour and a half, while the southern half near Cashel and the Cork border can stretch past two hours, so most Dublin bands can same-day it. Cork bands are even closer, often under an hour to Cashel, making overnight stays uncommon unless the venue is very rural.

venueNotes.name: Cashel Palace
venueNotes.note: A recently restored palace hotel in the shadow of the Rock; load-in needs to respect the historic fabric and narrow access.

venueNotes.name: Dundrum House
venueNotes.note: A Georgian country house with a generous ballroom set away from the main house; access is generally easy.

venueNotes.name: Bansha Castle
venueNotes.note: A private castle with a more intimate scale; the band setup needs to fit a smaller reception room.

venueNotes.name: Aherlow House
venueNotes.note: A country hotel beneath the Galtee Mountains with panoramic views; the drive up is steep and narrow in places.

localFaq.q: Do bands charge travel fees for Tipperary?
localFaq.a: Many Dublin and Cork bands include Tipperary in their standard travel area, but always confirm whether travel costs are built in or itemised.

localFaq.q: What's the best way to handle power at a rural Tipperary venue?
localFaq.a: Established venues have proper power, but if you're hiring a marquee or using a private house, arrange an electrician's sign-off and tell the band early.

localFaq.q: Can the band set up early if the ceremony and reception are at the same Tipperary venue?
localFaq.a: Yes, same-venue weddings make logistics easier, but the band still needs a clear window during room turnaround or a separate space to store cases.

planningNote: Tipperary's wedding calendar peaks from May through September, with Cashel and the mid-county estates drawing strong demand. The county's central location makes it a practical choice for families split between Dublin and Cork, which keeps Saturday dates competitive.

name: Waterford
intro: Waterford weddings centre on Faithlegg House, Cliff House, and Mount Congreve. A coastal-leaning county with both period-house formality and contemporary boutique options. Bands chosen here tend toward versatile and energetic rather than stately.
travelNote: The M9 from Dublin gets a band to Waterford city in about two to two-and-a-half hours, and Cork is roughly ninety minutes to the east, so many Waterford weddings are same-day returns. Venues along the Copper Coast or beyond Dungarvan add extra time on smaller roads and can tip the balance toward an overnight.

venueNotes.name: Faithlegg House
venueNotes.note: A country-house hotel with a riverside setting and a well-proportioned ballroom; load-in is straightforward.

venueNotes.name: Cliff House Hotel
venueNotes.note: A dramatic clifftop boutique hotel with compact spaces; the band needs to suit a smaller, design-led room.

venueNotes.name: Mount Congreve
venueNotes.note: A historic estate with gardens; marquee and outdoor receptions are common, so power and weather backup need planning.

venueNotes.name: Waterford Castle
venueNotes.note: An island castle reached by ferry; the band must coordinate ferry times carefully for load-in and load-out.

localFaq.q: How does the ferry work for a Waterford Castle wedding band?
localFaq.a: The island is reached by private ferry, so the band needs to know the timetable and allow buffer time; late finishes require a confirmed return crossing.

localFaq.q: Are Waterford venues strict on sound curfews?
localFaq.a: Coastal and residential venues can have earlier curfews; ask the venue for their music finish time and any sound-management policy.

localFaq.q: Do bands from Dublin need accommodation in Waterford?
localFaq.a: Usually not for city venues, but for Ardmore, the Copper Coast or very late finishes, an overnight room is often arranged.

planningNote: Waterford's wedding season runs from April through September, with summer Saturdays and bank-holiday weekends filling first. The county has a strong autumn-wedding appeal thanks to the gardens and softer coastal light.

name: Wexford
intro: Wexford is one of Ireland's quietly excellent wedding counties, Marlfield House, Brooklodge (just over the Wicklow border), Ferrycarrig. The wedding scene leans warm, coastal, and friendly, with a wedding crowd that responds well to harmony-driven bands.
travelNote: Dublin to Wexford town is roughly an hour and a half on the M11, and the county is a straightforward same-day return for most capital-based bands. The Hook Peninsula and south Wexford coast push the journey closer to two hours and can make an overnight worth considering for very late finishes.

venueNotes.name: Marlfield House
venueNotes.note: A Victorian country house with elegant, medium-sized reception rooms; the band needs to fit a refined space without overwhelming it.

venueNotes.name: Ferrycarrig Hotel
venueNotes.note: A modern hotel overlooking the River Slaney with level access and good parking for load-in.

venueNotes.name: Brooklodge
venueNotes.note: A mountain-valley hotel just over the Wicklow border; the winding approach means bands allow extra travel time.

venueNotes.name: Loftus Hall
venueNotes.note: A remote historic house on the Hook Peninsula; the band almost always stays overnight and coordinates road access carefully.

localFaq.q: Do Wexford venues charge extra for bands travelling from Dublin?
localFaq.a: Most Dublin bands include Wexford in their standard area, but the very south of the county or late finishes may attract a small travel supplement.

localFaq.q: Can we have a late licence at a Wexford country house?
localFaq.a: Licences vary by venue and location; rural venues near residential areas may have earlier curfews, so confirm the finish time in writing.

localFaq.q: Is it easy to load equipment into Loftus Hall?
localFaq.a: The remote location and historic building mean load-in needs advance planning; the band will usually ask for a site contact and approved access route.

planningNote: Wexford's wedding season peaks from May through September, with coastal and country-house venues drawing Dublin couples looking for a getaway feel. June and August are the busiest months, while spring and autumn can offer better availability.

name: Kilkenny
intro: Kilkenny's wedding circuit is led by Mount Juliet Estate, with Lyrath Estate and Newpark Hotel rounding out the higher end. Country-estate style dominates and bands chosen here tend toward the polished, big-vocal end of the spectrum.
travelNote: Dublin to Kilkenny is around an hour and a half on the M9, and Cork is roughly ninety minutes to the south, so most bands can same-day it. The county is compact, with even rural venues usually within half an hour of the city.

venueNotes.name: Mount Juliet Estate
venueNotes.note: A large estate with a dedicated ballroom; load-in is well organised and the events team manages timings.

venueNotes.name: Lyrath Estate
venueNotes.note: A modern country-house hotel with a grand ballroom and good access via the main drive.

venueNotes.name: Newpark Hotel
venueNotes.note: A city hotel with a contemporary function suite and convenient parking.

venueNotes.name: Kilkenny Hibernian
venueNotes.note: A boutique hotel in the city centre with a smaller, characterful room; best suited to a scaled-back band.

localFaq.q: Do Kilkenny wedding bands need accommodation?
localFaq.a: For city venues, usually not; for very late finishes or bands travelling from further afield, an overnight room may be requested.

localFaq.q: Can we fit a full band in the Kilkenny Hibernian?
localFaq.a: The room is more intimate, so many couples choose a smaller line-up or an acoustic-led band for that venue.

localFaq.q: What should we check with Kilkenny venues about evening noise?
localFaq.a: Some city hotels and residential areas manage sound levels; ask the venue directly and share the policy with your band.

planningNote: Kilkenny's wedding season runs from April through September, with Mount Juliet and Lyrath setting the pace for summer Saturdays. The city's compact nature and strong hotel stock make it popular for multi-day weddings and guest stays.

name: Carlow
intro: Carlow's wedding scene is anchored by the Lord Bagenal Inn, Mount Wolseley, and Step House Hotel, boutique-leaning rather than castle-dominant. The bands chosen here lean toward feel-good and warm rather than stately-formal.
travelNote: Carlow is roughly an hour to an hour and a half from Dublin on the M9 or M7, and about two hours from Cork, so Dublin bands usually treat it as a same-day return. The county is compact and its venues are close to the main road network.

venueNotes.name: Mount Wolseley Hotel
venueNotes.note: A modern hotel with spacious function rooms and straightforward loading access.

venueNotes.name: Lord Bagenal Inn
venueNotes.note: A boutique inn in Leighlinbridge with characterful, smaller rooms; the band needs to suit an intimate setting.

venueNotes.name: Step House Hotel
venueNotes.note: A stylish townhouse hotel in Borris with a warm, compact reception space.

venueNotes.name: Seven Oaks
venueNotes.note: A hotel on the edge of Carlow town with good parking and a practical function suite.

localFaq.q: Is Carlow a good choice for a band travelling from Dublin?
localFaq.a: Yes, the short run down the M9 makes it an easy same-day return for most Dublin-based bands, with minimal travel supplement.

localFaq.q: Do small Carlow venues suit a full live band?
localFaq.a: Some boutique venues are better suited to a scaled-back line-up; discuss room size and the band's footprint before booking.

localFaq.q: What time does music usually finish at Carlow hotels?
localFaq.a: Most town hotels have standard late licences, but confirm the curfew with your venue as it can vary by location.

planningNote: Carlow's wedding season follows the Leinster pattern, peaking from May through September. The county's affordability and proximity to Dublin make it popular with couples who want a country feel without a long guest journey.

name: Kildare
intro: Kildare's wedding venue circuit is led by The K Club, Carton House and Barberstown Castle, estate luxury within an easy distance of Dublin. The wedding crowd skews ambitious and the bands need the scale to match.
travelNote: Kildare venues are rarely more than an hour from Dublin city centre, with many sitting just off the M4, M7 or M9 within twenty to fifty minutes of the M50. Same-day returns are standard, and even late finishes still allow an easy run back to the capital.

venueNotes.name: The K Club
venueNotes.note: A five-star estate with a refined ballroom and a well-drilled events team; load-in is managed to the minute.

venueNotes.name: Carton House
venueNotes.note: A grand country house with multiple event spaces; confirm which room is allocated and the closest drop-off point.

venueNotes.name: Barberstown Castle
venueNotes.note: A castle hotel with a warm, medieval-meets-modern atmosphere; the reception room suits a lively band.

venueNotes.name: Killashee Hotel
venueNotes.note: A Victorian hotel set in parkland with a large ballroom and plenty of parking.

venueNotes.name: Cliff at Lyons
venueNotes.note: A restored canal-side village with intimate, design-led spaces; a smaller band line-up fits best.

localFaq.q: Do Kildare bands charge travel fees from Dublin?
localFaq.a: Most Kildare venues are so close to Dublin that travel is included in the base rate; always confirm if your venue is on the border of a band's standard area.

localFaq.q: Can the band set up early at a Kildare venue?

name: Fermanagh
intro: Fermanagh's wedding scene is led by Lough Erne Resort, a Ryder Cup-style luxury venue with a strong international wedding crowd. Plus a quieter circuit of country houses and lakeside hotels.
travelNote: Fermanagh is about an hour and a half from Belfast and two to two and a half hours from Dublin on the A4 and N16, so bands usually treat it as an overnight trip. The lakeland setting and cross-border currency difference are the two practical details to confirm with a Republic-based band.

venueNotes.name: Lough Erne Resort
venueNotes.note: A five-star lakeland resort with high production standards; the events team coordinates load-in, staging and timing closely.

venueNotes.name: Manor House Country Hotel
venueNotes.note: A country hotel on the shores of Lower Lough Erne with a warm ballroom; the scenic approach includes narrow lakeside roads.

venueNotes.name: Killyhevlin Lakeside Hotel
venueNotes.note: A modern hotel on the edge of Enniskillen with good access and parking; the function suite suits a lively band.

localFaq.q: Do Fermanagh venues have boat access for wedding bands?
localFaq.a: Boat transfers are rarely practical for equipment; plan a standard road load-in and treat any boat element as a guest experience rather than band transport.

localFaq.q: Should we book accommodation for the band at Lough Erne Resort?
localFaq.a: Yes, the distance from Dublin and Belfast and the likelihood of a late finish mean an overnight room is standard.

localFaq.q: How does currency work when booking a Republic band for a Fermanagh wedding?
localFaq.a: Northern Ireland uses sterling, so confirm whether the band quotes in euro or sterling and how payment will be handled.

localFaq.q: Are Fermanagh lakeland venues strict on sound curfews?
localFaq.a: Lakeside and rural venues can have noise restrictions; ask the venue directly about their music finish time and any sound-management policy.

planningNote: Fermanagh's wedding season runs from April through September, with Lough Erne Resort and the lakeland hotels drawing most of the summer demand. The county's international wedding crowd and tight Saturday availability mean top venues book out well ahead.

name: Derry
intro: Derry/Londonderry weddings range from urban venues in the city to country-house options across the county. Live wedding bands from across the island travel to Derry regularly.
travelNote: Derry is roughly an hour and a half from Belfast and two and a half to three hours from Dublin, so Republic-based bands usually need an overnight. Donegal and Tyrone bands are closer, and the city itself has good loading access at the hotels.

venueNotes.name: Beech Hill Country House
venueNotes.note: A country-house hotel just outside the city with a relaxed atmosphere and a compact reception room; a scaled-back band line-up suits it well.

venueNotes.name: Bishop's Gate Hotel
venueNotes.note: A boutique hotel inside the historic city walls with stylish function spaces; loading access and parking need advance agreement.

venueNotes.name: Da Vinci's Hotel
venueNotes.note: A modern hotel near the river with a large function suite and good parking.

localFaq.q: Do Republic-based bands charge extra to play in Derry?
localFaq.a: The longer cross-border drive and overnight mean most bands add a travel supplement; confirm whether the quote is in euro or sterling.

localFaq.q: Is Derry easy for Belfast bands to reach?
localFaq.a: Yes, Belfast is only about an hour and a half away, so many Derry weddings are same-day returns for Belfast-based bands.

localFaq.q: What should couples ask Derry venues about late licences?
localFaq.a: City hotels and country houses can have different curfews; confirm the music finish time and any sound-management policy before booking.

localFaq.q: Can the band set up early if our ceremony and reception are both at Beech Hill?
localFaq.a: Same-venue weddings simplify logistics, but the band still needs a clear window during room turnaround or a secure storage space.

planningNote: Derry's wedding season runs from April through September, with city-centre and country-house venues drawing couples from across the north west. The county's strong cultural scene makes live music popular, and summer Saturdays book up ahead of the rest of the year.
